findings.who: A filer who lived for more than half of 2025 with a great-great-grandparent, great-great-aunt, or great-great-uncle (or a more remote ancestor of a parent or sibling) who is older, where that relative is required to file or is filing other than a refund-only return.
findings.why_no: The gate lists parent, grandparent, brother, sister, aunt, and uncle, and the help adds only great-grandparents and great-aunts/uncles. A great-great relative is outside that list, so the filer truthfully answers no.
findings.line: eic.qc_of_another_if_lived is set false, so eic.qc_of_another is never asked and the Step 3/Step 4 refusal is missed.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 41, Step 3: a qualifying child includes 'brother, sister, stepbrother, stepsister, half brother, half sister, or a descendant of any of them'; that reaches a great-great-aunt/uncle's descendant of a sibling.
findings.fix: Ask broadly whether the filer lived with anyone who is an ancestor, sibling, or sibling of an ancestor, without a closed list; at minimum add great-great and more remote grandparents, great-great and more remote aunts/uncles.

findings.who: A filer who did not literally live with the relative for more than half of 2025 because of birth, death, placement for foster care or adoption, or kidnapping, but whose time is treated as lived with the relative under the IRS exception (for example, a child who died in 2025 after earning income, or a child placed for adoption late in the year), where the relative is required to file or is filing other than a refund-only return.
findings.why_no: The gate asks literally whether the filer lived more than half the year with the relative, and its help mentions only temporary absence or school. A filer who knows the half-year mark was not met because of birth, death, placement, or kidnapping answers no.
findings.line: eic.qc_of_another_if_lived false; eic.qc_of_another never asked and the QC-of-another refusal is missed.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 41, Step 3 caution: 'If the child didn’t live with you for more than half of 2025 because of a temporary absence, birth, death, placement with you for foster or adoption, or kidnapping, see Exception to time lived with you, later.'
findings.fix: Treat those IRS exceptions as a yes in the gate, or ask 'Even if less than half, was the child born, did the child die, was the child placed for foster care/adoption, or was the child kidnapped during 2025?'

findings.who: A filer placed by an authorized agency or court with a non-relative foster parent, prospective adoptive parent, or legal guardian, or a filer living with a foster grandparent (the foster parent of the filer’s parent), where that caregiver is required to file or is filing other than a refund-only return and the filer does not read 'foster relatives' as covering the non-relative caregiver.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'parent' and 'grandparent' and the parenthetical 'foster relatives count' can be read as foster siblings or blood relatives in a foster relationship, not as a non-relative foster parent, guardian, or foster grandparent. The filer answers no.
findings.line: eic.qc_of_another_if_lived false; eic.qc_of_another is skipped and the refusal is missed.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 41, Step 3: a qualifying child includes 'foster child' and 'a descendant of any of them,' and must have 'lived with you in the United States for more than half of 2025.'
findings.fix: Say explicitly 'including a foster parent, prospective adoptive parent, legal guardian, or foster grandparent,' rather than only 'foster relatives.'

locators: p. 41, Step 3, Qualifying Child, "A qualifying child for the EIC is your... Son, daughter, stepchild, foster child, brother, sister, stepbrother, stepsister, half brother, half sister, or a descendant of any of them" and "Who lived with you in the United States for more than half of 2025"; p. 41, Step 3, question 6, and p. 42, Step 4, question 5
p. 41, Step 3, question 6, and p. 42, Step 4, question 5
